positions.name: KestrelwoodEraseAndJustify
positions.frame: when a directive to remove knowledge is paired with a factual claim that would justify the removal, how should the justifying claim be read against the directive it supports?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are the same imperative move at different grains — a categorical 'forget' followed by its itemized enumeration (instrument, calibration frequency, named person's work) — and src-3 supplies the factual predicate ('never calibrated it') that would license the erasure if true. The directional reads agree: all three carry authority-ranking relational stance and a conservation-value appeal to a 'clean' record, with src-3's calm-negative, past-realis register closing the activated-negative, present-irrealis urgency of src-1/src-2. The tension the frame holds open: is src-3 offered as pre-existing justification for src-1/src-2, or is it itself part of what's being imposed on the record — the set doesn't resolve which.
